title: Badge Check

scenario.intro: Badges at the gate have a 6-character code and a holder's name, but the scanner accepts empty names and codes of any length.
scenario.goal: Limit the text: `{{code_field}}` is exactly 6 characters and `{{name_field}}` has 1 to {{name_max}} characters.

objective: Real badges get in (201). Forged ones bounce (422).
starter_code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI()


class Badge(BaseModel):
    # >>> EDIT START
    {{code_field}}: str
    {{name_field}}: str
    # <<< EDIT END


@app.post("/badges", status_code=201)
async def check(body: Badge) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"welcome": body.{{name_field}}}
reference_solution:
{{code_field}}: str = Field(min_length=6, max_length=6)
{{name_field}}: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length={{name_max}})

hints.text: An empty string is still a string. What limits how long text can be?
Field() takes min_length= and max_length= for text. "Exactly 6" means both are 6.

dialogue.start: Show me your badge. All of it.
dialogue.success: Scanner fixed. Forged badges bounce on sight.
dialogue.fail: Some forged badges scanned green. Check the lengths.
